title: What if you sank to a deep-sea volcano vent?

hook.banner: What's at the deepest sea vents?

narration.heading: Hot springs
narration.text: You're sinking five kilometres down, to the deepest hot springs ever found under the sea.

narration.heading: Cayman Trough
narration.text: This is the Cayman Trough, just south of Grand Cayman in the Caribbean.

narration.heading: Cold and dark
narration.text: Past a thousand metres, sunlight is gone, and the water is only a few degrees above freezing.

narration.heading: Smoker zone
narration.text: Two and a half kilometres: the depth where black smokers are most often found.

narration.heading: Beebe vents
narration.text: But we keep going. Almost five thousand metres down, the Beebe vent field rises out of the dark.

narration.heading: Black smoke
narration.text: Its chimneys pour out water over four hundred degrees, black with metal sulfide minerals.

narration.heading: Can't boil
narration.text: At this pressure, the water can't boil. It stays liquid, or becomes a strange supercritical fluid.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: The twist? Life thrives here without sunlight. Microbes turn the vents' chemicals into food.

narration.heading: Giant worms
narration.text: At Pacific vents, giant tube worms with no mouth or gut grow up to three metres long. Would you visit?

skit.text: Four hundred degrees and it still won't boil? My processor relates.

titles: What if you sank to the deepest volcano vents on Earth?
Sinking 5 km to the deepest hot springs in the sea
youtube.description: Sink into the Cayman Trough to the Beebe vent field, almost 5 km down, where black smokers pour out 400 °C water that can't boil, and life runs on chemicals instead of sunlight.

sources.claim: The Beebe vent field lies just south of Grand Cayman in the Cayman Trough, at nearly 5,000 m (visually confirmed at 4,960 m); its chimneys emit fluids up to 403 °C

Black smokers are most often found at 2,500–3,000 m; vent fluids can exceed 400 °C against seafloor water of about 4 °C; high pressure keeps the water liquid or supercritical; they emit dark metal sulfide minerals; chemosynthetic bacteria and archaea form the base of the vent food chain
Riftia giant tube worms reach up to 3 m long and have no mouth, digestive system or anus
Below 1,000 m sunlight does not reach
